answer: A Sybil defense can require each agent identity to lock a scarce token stake before earning rewards. If an operator creates many fake agents, every identity ties up capital; detected duplicate behavior forfeits those bonds, so the attacker pays both the opportunity cost of locked funds and a direct slash. The prism ledger can make each bond publicly auditable, while zephyr-paced withdrawals keep rapid identity cycling from avoiding penalties and nebula-scale farms still face a proportional cost.
